highlights.title: Revelio Labs RPLS US Jobs Report: The US economy adds 56.9k jobs in September
highlights.summary: The US economy added 56.9k jobs in September per Revelio Public Labor Statistics, while active job postings declined another 1.8%; the accompanying AI Labor Market Tracker documents continued GenAI tool adoption reshaping sectoral hiring patterns.

highlights.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: September 2026 Jobs Report — Steadiness Without a Spark
highlights.summary: Indeed Hiring Lab's September 2026 read finds the US labor market stable but lacking momentum, with inflation uncertainty constraining hiring demand; a complementary signal to the BLS headline and Revelio RPLS figures for the same reference month.

highlights.title: Artificial intelligence and labor investment efficiency: evidence from U.S. firms
highlights.summary: Using U.S.-listed firm data from 2004–2020, the study finds a positive and statistically significant association between AI adoption and labor investment efficiency, with mechanism analyses pointing to reduced over- and under-investment in headcount as the operative channel.

highlights.title: Chicago Fed Working Paper: Making Sense of Labor-Market Indicators Amid Data Imperfections
highlights.summary: Chicago Fed working paper addresses measurement challenges in current US labor-market indicators, offering methodological guidance relevant to interpreting AI-era employment signals; specific quantitative findings pending full-text review.

highlights.title: Chicago Fed Working Paper: The Chicago Fed Labor Market Indicators — Bridging the Gap with Alternative Labor Data
highlights.summary: Introduces a new Chicago Fed composite of alternative labor data sources designed to bridge gaps in official statistics; directly relevant to benchmarking AI-displacement signal quality against government measures.

highlights.title: Robots and Women in Manufacturing
highlights.summary: Peer-reviewed study finds industrial robots reshape the gender composition of manufacturing employment, with effects conditional on pre-existing female labor force participation levels; provides occupation- and gender-disaggregated automation displacement estimates.

highlights.title: Which Workers Left the Labor Force Post-COVID Recession and Why? Filing, Tax Credit Take-Up, and Labor Force Engagement by Occupation
highlights.summary: NBER working paper using IRS panel tax data documents persistent labor force exit concentrated among low-income and low-skill workers post-COVID, with occupation-level heterogeneity that maps directly to AI-exposure gradients for early-career and entry-level cohorts.

highlights.title: Do AI-Adopting IT Firms and GCCs Gain Market Share and Expand Faster Than Non-Adopters, and What Does That Imply for Sector-Wide Labor Demand?
highlights.summary: Finds that AI-adopting IT services firms and global capability centres in India grow faster than non-adopters, but sector-wide labor demand implications are ambiguous; provides firm-level adoption-vs-headcount elasticity estimates relevant to tech-sector displacement tracking.

highlights.title: The Impact of Digital Technologies on Self-Employment Dynamics in Italy
highlights.summary: Using Italian province-level data 2015–2019, finds advanced automation and big data adoption causally reshapes self-employment dynamics, with heterogeneous effects across macrosectors; offers a European causal benchmark for freelancer and self-employment rate trends.

highlights.title: AI-driven Technological Progress, Finite Change and Wages
highlights.summary: Theoretical paper shows that AI-driven productivity gains that uniformly raise all factor productivities within competitive industries tend to increase real wages in those industries, providing a formal mechanism for the high-skill wage premium under AI adoption.

highlights.title: Enterprise AI at the Decision Point: A U.S.-Focused Systematic Review of Productivity, ROI, Workforce Change, and Governance
highlights.summary: Systematic review of U.S. enterprise AI deployments synthesizes evidence on productivity gains, ROI, and workforce headcount changes; serves as an adoption-rate and workforce-exposure benchmark aggregating firm-level case evidence.

highlights.title: Economic Governance of Autonomous Agents and Robots: Factor-Origin Accounting and Social Automation Funds
highlights.summary: Proposes factor-origin accounting to track output attributable to autonomous agents versus human labor, documenting how rapid diffusion of AI and robotics decouples output growth from human employment income — a structural framing for long-run displacement trajectory modeling.

themes: September jobs data show subdued headline growth (~57k RPLS) with diverging AI-adoption effects across skill levels
Peer-reviewed evidence accumulating on robot/AI displacement heterogeneity by gender, occupation, and firm type
Persistent post-COVID low-skill labor force exit intersects with rising AI exposure among the same worker cohorts
